title: Room prose names verbs the action surface rejects
body:
PARTLY FIXED. The larger half — the missing inline action ids — is resolved; the
narration half remains open.

WHAT WAS WRONG

`defaultCompactRpg` and `defaultCompactOverworldAndRpg` in src/mcp/server.ts set
`include_actions: true` only when PLAY_MODE === "pure". Every other caller — a person, a
dev-loop agent, a hand-driven MCP session like the three playtest leads in the live run —
received observations with no legal action ids and had to call `list_legal_actions`
before nearly every step. One lead measured roughly a third of its tool calls as that
overhead rather than play.

It was not a considered trade-off, which the numbers settle. Measured on a fresh session:

  include_actions inline        +48 chars on an observation (+16%), no extra round trip
  separate list_legal_actions    89 chars, PLUS a whole round trip

Inline is about half the payload AND saves a turn. There was no case for the asymmetry;
pure play simply got the fix and nobody else did.

Both defaults now set it for non-pure callers, with an explicit `include_actions` from
the caller still winning. Verified through the live MCP server: `get_observation` with no
arguments returns `"actions":["go_down","look_around","inventory"]` in its context.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN

The other half of the original finding is untouched: room prose names actions in a
vocabulary the action surface does not accept. A lead found the Store-Shed saying "DON
padded byre-jerkin" when the only legal action is `take_byre_jerkin`; following the text
produces a flat rejection. Inline ids make that recoverable rather than fatal — the
correct id is now on screen — but a player who reads carefully and types what the prose
told them still gets refused, which is a comprehension defect in its own right.

Two directions, both still open:
  - Bring narration verbs and action ids into one vocabulary, so following the prose
    works.
  - Or have a rejected near-miss name the closest legal id in its message, turning a
    wasted call into a correction.

MEASUREMENT

Recomputable from stored transcripts: the share of tool calls in a session that are
`list_legal_actions` or `get_observation` versus state-advancing actions. Worth running
against the corpus before and after, so the improvement is a number rather than an
impression. No corpus predating this change has been kept, so the baseline to compare
against is the next live cohort.

evidence.summary: Inline action ids fixed (measured: half the payload, one fewer round trip); the prose/action vocabulary mismatch is still open.
